title: Seat Reservation

functional: Browse events and a live seat map with availability.
Hold one or more seats for a short, visible expiry window.
Confirm a reservation with payment and issue a booking.
Support cancellation and refunds according to the event policy.
Release expired holds automatically and publish every state change.
nonFunctional: Never sell the same seat twice, even during a traffic spike.
Seat-map reads should stay fast under heavy read traffic.
A hold must expire reliably within a few seconds of its deadline.
A payment-provider outage must not corrupt seat state or lose a paid booking.
Every hold, sale, release, and refund must be auditable.

checklist: Seat inventory model and uniqueness constraint
Hold lifecycle, expiry, and automatic release
Read path, caching, and hot-event handling
Failure modes for payment, cache, worker, and database outages
Trade-offs: consistency, latency, and operational complexity
followUps: How would you support general-admission events without individual seats?
How would you handle a queue or waiting room for a very popular on-sale?
What changes if seats can be transferred between users after purchase?
How would you migrate seat inventory between database shards during an on-sale?
commonMistakes: Checking availability and writing the sale in two separate transactions.
Relying on a cache as the source of truth for seat ownership.
Charging the card before the seat is durably reserved.
Expiring holds with a periodic scan that has no lease or idempotency.
Ignoring duplicate confirm requests caused by client retries.
